statement: For boosted trees (scikit-learn's HistGradientBoosting) and XGBoost under prediction, when the effective size of one outer training fold (n_plan: units for a numeric outcome; units in the rarest class for a yes/no or class outcome) is below 300, fitting once at the library's default settings with no search (HistGB: learning rate 0.1, 31 leaves, smallest leaf 20, no L2, 100 trees; XGBoost: learning rate 0.3, depth 6, child weight 1, λ 1, 100 rounds) predicts at least as well as nested tuning and is better calibrated, because settings ranked on so few units vary from sample to sample and miscalibrate.
regime: Prediction; boosted trees and XGBoost; n_plan < 300 (e.g. fewer than 375 events in the training set at K = 5); any outcome type
decision: Tuning plan below n_eff 300: no Sobol candidates (S = 0); the library defaults are the only candidate
user_sees: Boosted trees' methods text: "scikit-learn's defaults (100 trees of at most 31 leaves) always among them and used alone below an effective size of 300 (units, events or the rarest class's count)."

statement: Under inference with repeated units at or above the unit floor, GEE with an exchangeable working correlation and CR2 (bias-reduced linearization) intervals on Bell–McCaffrey degrees of freedom gives near-nominal type I error even with about 12 units, and below the unit floor its intervals are refused with the mixed model as the exit.
regime: Inference; continuous or binary outcome; repeated units
decision: GEE table intervals, refusal below the floor, and its shelf score
user_sees: "Rows repeat within only 6 units, fewer than the 8 a sandwich interval needs; a random-intercept mixed model can."
claimed_basis: Liang & Zeger 1986; McCaffrey & Bell, Stat Med 2006;25:4081 (BRL); unit floor = seal.min_groups() = 8 (utils/test_lockbox.py:70).
notes: [part id F2-031] Test: 12 units, 300 replicates, rejection ≤ 8%. The floor's value lives in seal.py (outside this area).

decision: no resampling or class weighting by default; the sentence beside every binary fit
user_sees: "The event, `case`, is 12% of the training rows. No resampling (SMOTE, over- or undersampling) or class weighting was applied: customary in machine-learning papers, resampling overestimates the rar...
claimed_basis: van den Goorbergh et al., JAMIA 2022;29:1525 (quoted).
notes: [part id F5-017] BUG-LIKE: the sentence is emitted unconditionally for binary fits, even when Explore's imbalance lever (decisions.py:1712: weights/undersample/oversample, with recalibration) is on, so it can state that no resampling was applied when it was. test_wp9_validation_performance.py::test_e15 pins wording only. [Merged P-class-reweighting-wrong-probabilities at docs/turbotab-next/RECIPES_AND_TUNING.md §0 ('Breaking defaults', item 3), §2.2 XGBoost, §7.3 'Impossible by construction'; its basis: None cited in RECIPES; methods/levers.py ImbalanceCorrected recalibrates.; its notes: 'Every predicted probability wrong' is the doc's wording (§0); the precise claim is that probabilities are miscalibrated toward the reweighted prior.]

statement: Before the lock under Estimate, the share of rows an exclusion rule (an energy-intake screen) removes, multiplied by the largest standardized mean difference (Austin 2009; pooled-SD for numbers, per-level proportion difference for categories) between the removed and kept rows on the adjustment set, is an outcome-blind predictor of how far keeping every row would move the exposure's estimate in units of its 95% interval half-width, good enough to band the noticing as doesn't change / could bias / act on it.
regime: Dietary lens; Estimate or Describe; an energy screen (Goldberg, or a range rule on the energy column) among the exclusions; before the plan's lock
decision: Predicted band and recommended triage disposition of the implausible-reporters noticing
user_sees: "The energy screen removes `412` of `5,000` rows (8.2%), who differ from the others by up to 0.31 standard deviations in `age`, which the model adjusts for." with label "rows × SMD = 0.082 × 0.310 = 0.025"
claimed_basis: SURFACING_POLICY §2.3 item 2 (design-space movement, 'rows lost × max |SMD|', the shared-missingness-mechanism rank signal); Austin 2009 for SMD; 9 calibration cases in materiality_calibration.json
notes: [part id F6-006] Also materiality.py:255-283 (smd), 705-733 (reporters_noticing). The repo's own test test_materiality_dietary_proof.py::test_a_narrow_screen_once_said_to_change_nothing_could_bias_and_is_upgraded_openly documents a case with rows×SMD ≈ 0.019 realized at 0.63 half-widths (high-leverage extreme reports), and the committed cases are not monotone (0.0037→0.20, 0.185→0.124, 0.149→0.545). The proxy ignores how leavers differ in exposure and outcome, which is what moves the estimate. test_materiality.py::test_rows_times_smd_is_the_share_leaving_times_the_largest_standardized_difference checks arithmetic only.

statement: Restricting the analysis to consumers (exposure > 0) changes the estimand to the effect among consumers rather than in the whole population. It is therefore recorded as an estimand change (STROBE-nut nut-14), offered only under inference and only for the declared exposure. It is refused under prediction because the model is applied to everyone.
regime: inference (refused under prediction); declared exposure with zeros
user_sees: "A consumers-only domain changes the population the estimate is about; under prediction the model is used on everyone, consumers or not."
claimed_basis: STROBE-nut (Lachat et al. 2016) nut-14; MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 row 2 and §2 ("Zeros in a food exposure")
notes: The test_form_6 tests are refusal and caption checks. Option text at :1101: "Answers a different question: the effect among consumers, not in everyone." Record sentence is at :2069.

statement: Absolute risks cannot be predicted from individually matched case-control sets, as a limit of the design: the conditional likelihood removes every set's intercept so there is no baseline risk to recalibrate, and matched controls are not a random sample of non-cases, so no single offset turns the sample's odds into anyone's risk.
user_sees: Risks cannot be predicted from individually matched sets. The analysis within each set leaves no baseline risk to recalibrate… This is a limit of the design, not a missing feature.

statement: When the marginal risk difference or ratio is declared, the unmeasured-confounding E-value is computed on the marginal risk ratio with its bootstrap limits rather than on the conditional odds ratio, since a risk difference has no E-value without its risks.
regime: inference; binary outcome; marginal measure declared
user_sees: E-value for the marginal risk ratio: ..., and for the confidence limit nearer the null ...
notes: test_estimand_2_g_computation.py::test_2_below_the_unit_floor... checks the computed value only. Also turbotab/core/models/effects.py:1096-1097, turbotab/core/stages/effects.py:1496-1498.

statement: When matching was within a range (a matching factor differs within some sets), conditional logistic regression does not remove what the matching left, which may confound a little.
regime: individually matched sets with a range-matched factor
user_sees: age differs within some sets (matching within a range): what the matching left is not removed by the analysis and may confound a little.

statement: For a time-to-event outcome under prediction with no declared prediction horizon, scoring predicted risk (Brier score and calibration) at the median follow-up time of the training rows is an appropriate default horizon.
regime: Time-to-event outcome; prediction; no prediction horizon declared
decision: Horizon at which risk predictions are scored and calibrated
user_sees: Stated in the record: "Calibration read at the median follow-up time (no horizon was declared)"; the horizon changes the Brier score and calibration
claimed_basis: METHODS_REFERENCE contract horizon_calibration: 'stated: the prediction horizon is declared with the follow-up, else the median follow-up time'
notes: Merges crosswalk default:prediction_horizon and default:horizon_calibration. No UI control sets the horizon. test_ms6_prediction_validation.py::test_1_the_brier_score_at_the_horizon_matches_graf_and_r_survival and ::test_5_calibration_at_the_horizon_matches_r_survival check the computation at a given horizon against R, not the choice of the median. | Inventory source id: CW-003.

statement: An energy source's amounts are settled as grams by the Atwater identity only where it excludes every other unit: the identity passes (ratio 0.90-1.10) with the column read in grams, the column is not alcohol (standard drinks hold 8-20 g by country and alcohol is a minor source), the column carries at least 1 - 1/1.10 (about 9%) of reconstructed energy on the median row (below that any unit, or none, keeps the ratio in band), and reading it in kg, kcal or kJ instead moves the ratio out of band; otherwise a substitution or partition waits for the user's recorded unit.
regime: Dietary substitution / partition energy models; macronutrient energy sources.
decision: kcal per unit used to move energy through a source in substitution and partition models.
user_sees: "`protein_g` carries about 3% of the energy its macronutrients reconstruct, below the 9% the identity's 0.90-1.10 band can see: in another unit, or missing, the identity would hold as well"
claimed_basis: BLUEPRINT §14.3 (sixth gate: US standard drinks reconstructed at 1.02 read as grams; an InBody Protein confirmed in kg moved energy at 4 kcal per unit); Kalinowski & Humphreys 2016 Addiction 111:1293 (8-20 g); NUTRITION_PACK §01.
notes: MINOR_SHARE readings.py:928, DRINK_GRAMS :934, KIND_RULES unit:factor :1241; kcal_per_unit :2312. The ~9% floor assumes every other source is exact; with the ratio near 0.90 or 1.10 already, the true detectable share differs. | Inventory source id: F3-028.

statement: An outcome over follow-up (a time-to-event task, a binary outcome whose name says incident/onset/new/developed/conversion, or an outcome named as follow-up, change, delta, endline, final, or with a time since baseline such as 12m/5y/24wk) implies the covariates were measured at baseline, before the outcome; occasion labels such as v1, t0 or w2 do not, because they may be the baseline itself.
decision: Switches covariate guesses between 'another measure of the outcome' (left out) and the with-and-without pair.
user_sees: The guess reason says "measured at baseline with what you study" vs "measured at the same visit as what you study".
claimed_basis: BLUEPRINT §14 (the name only leads a guess the user confirms); no methods source for the timing inference.
notes: Token sets covariate_guesses.py:210-217 (_INCIDENT, _FOLLOW_UP, _SINCE). A guess only, but it flips the pre-filled adjustment answers. | Inventory source id: F3-047.

statement: In a dietary analysis with total energy in the outcome model (standard model, or residual method with energy kept), a nutrient's coefficient estimates a substitution: more of that nutrient in place of the same energy from the energy sources not in the model, at fixed total energy, not the effect of simply eating more of it; with several energy sources in the model, 'everything else' is only the sources left out.
regime: dietary lens; nutrient exposures; a total-energy column in the outcome model; linear model
decision: how every energy-adjusted coefficient, estimand caption and energy finding is read
user_sees: An energy-adjusted coefficient is a substitution estimate: more of this nutrient and correspondingly less of everything else, at the same total intake — not the effect of simply eating more of it.
notes: Same claim at content.py:155-162 (LENS dietary), 1034-1038 (energy why), 1397-1402 (estimand drawer), 1219 (substitution why), terms 1070-1071 and 1079-1080 ('every swap is partly in its place'); finding_words.py:579-586 ('adjusting still makes each effect a swap at fixed energy'); voice.py:1334-1335 and 1490-1493 (omitted sources: 'the curve carries the confounding of the sources total energy holds as one composite'). The test covers only the omitted-sources part (a two-nutrient swap is biased; four sources recover the truth). The substitution reading assumes a linear, additive model; with splines or non-identity links it is conditional on the other intakes.

statement: Under Predict with a period held out, R² on the opened period computed against that period's own mean is conventional and conservative, and the comparison with a deployable baseline is the RMSE against the development mean's RMSE.
regime: prediction; a sealed latest period (NHANES glucose capture)
decision: the opened cycle's R² in Results
user_sees: R² on the opened cycle is computed against the cycle's own mean (0.18): conventional and conservative.
notes: Contradicts the engine (voice.py:1210; test_modeling.py:213 'not the held-out rows' own') and BEATS_PREDICT R5 Table 2 ('R² 0.20 ... against the development mean'). An own-mean R² ignores calibration-in-the-large; 'conservative' holds only when the period's mean differs from the development mean.

statement: When an intake screen would remove more than half the rows, the column's unit (kJ, a multi-day total, a child's or athlete's intake) is the likelier error rather than the people, so the screens refuse to remove more than half the rows until the unit is stated.
decision: the screens' refusal and the unit question
user_sees: When a screen would remove more than half the rows, the unit is the likelier error, not the people
notes: Also coach.py:659-664 ('check the unit'). The 50% threshold is a heuristic.

statement: A prediction model that reads a predictor known only after its intended moment of use looks better in a paper than in use, so only predictors recorded at that moment are read (e.g., no 24-hour recall for a clinic use).
regime: prediction; intended use and moment of use
user_sees: A model that reads something known only after its moment looks better in a paper than in use (PROBAST, Wolff et al. 2019, item 2.3).
